findings.rationale: The retained rebuilt wheel and shipped wheel are byte-identical at SHA-256 882b2f9d13fb16a2a756c21e73d3758789c1f5084129cdef3ae349ca4c8cb773, but their milai payload contains four files absent from current-source: milai/py.typed, milai/static/milai.css, milai/static/milai.js, and milai/templates/index.html. The wheel has 65 milai payload files while current-source/runtime/src/milai has 61, with exactly those four missing. The build configuration packages src/milai, Flask explicitly uses the missing static/templates directories, and the UI route renders the missing index.html. The closure builder only inventories runtime/src/**/*.py, so it silently excludes package-data inputs. Neither the 379-entry runner/helper closure nor the 418-entry source inventory contains these assets. Therefore the claimed independent rebuild was performed from a richer, unmaterialized filesystem state and cannot be reproduced from the closed candidate bytes. This leaves the parent R2 hermeticity finding open despite the valid captures and BFCL tracked-tree remediation.
findings.required_action: Materialize the four exact source assets under current-source/runtime/src/milai, change the R2 closure builder to inventory every wheel input including non-Python package data, rebuild the wheel from only the materialized source in a fresh environment, and regenerate the wheel, R2 closure, source/environment/authorization identities, R2 stage bindings and ledger checkpoint, and immutable review bundle. Do not authorize any model call meanwhile.
findings.title: Runtime wheel contains four unmaterialized source assets
